threads_text: Google's privacy policy now lets your Gmail, Drive and Photos content shape ads, but only if you connect those apps to its AI features like Personal Intelligence. The no ads promise it made in 2021 now comes with an exception. Is a smarter assistant worth more personal ads?
caption:
Google updated its privacy policy on October 16.
Its promise not to use Gmail, Drive or Photos content for ads now has an exception: when you connect those apps to its AI features, like Personal Intelligence.
Google says advertisers still cannot see your inbox or photos.

Would you keep Personal Intelligence turned on?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: PPC Land · Photo: SammyGuru

slides.headline: Google's 5-year promise just got an exception: your *Gmail and Photos* can now shape your ads

slides.heading: The *one sentence* that changed
paras: Since July 2021, Google's privacy policy promised no personalized ads based on your Drive, Gmail or Google Photos content.
On October 16, Google added an exception: unless you share that data with Google services that support personalized ads.

slides.heading: The *AI feature* behind it
paras: Personal Intelligence lets Search and Gemini draw on your connected Gmail, Photos and other apps. It is opt-in.
Google's help page says that same info "may be used to show you ads, so they are even more helpful for you."

slides.heading: What Google *still promises*
paras: Google says ads will not be based directly on your inbox or photo library, and advertisers get no access to either.
It also still bans ads based on sensitive categories like race, religion or health.

slides.heading: How to *turn it off*
paras: In your Google Account, open Search Services Personalization, then Connected Content Apps, and disconnect Gmail, Workspace or Photos.

paras.t: Disconnecting does not delete data Google already saved.

slides.hook: Follow so you know the next time Big Tech rewrites the rules on your data.

site_article.headline: Google adds an exception to its promise not to use Gmail and Photos content for ads
site_article.dek: The October 16 privacy policy lets content shape ads when users connect those apps to Google services such as Personal Intelligence.
site_article.summary: Google's privacy policy dated October 16, 2026, adds an exception to a 2021 pledge not to personalize ads using content from Drive, Gmail or Google Photos. The exception covers users who make that data available to Google services that support personalized ads, such as Search through Personal Intelligence.
site_article.seo_title: Google policy lets Gmail and Photos data shape ads via AI
site_article.seo_description: Google's October 16 privacy policy adds an exception: Gmail, Drive and Photos content connected to its AI features can personalize ads.
site_article.answer_summary: Google now allows content from Gmail, Drive and Google Photos to personalize ads, but only for users who connect those apps to Google services that support personalized ads, such as Search with Personal Intelligence. Google says ads are not based directly on the inbox and advertisers cannot see it.

paragraphs.text: Google has added an exception to a privacy promise it first made in July 2021, that it would not show personalized ads based on content from Drive, Gmail or Google Photos. The version of its privacy policy that took effect on October 16, 2026, keeps that promise in general but says it does not apply when users choose to make data from those services available to other Google services that support personalized ads, according to PPC Land and AndroidPure.

The change was first reported by Android Authority, according to Dexerto, and was covered by several technology outlets on October 23, 2026. The previous version of the policy was dated October 1, 2026, so the exception arrived 15 days later.

PPC Land, which compared archived versions of the policy, reported that the new text also gives an example: Search may process some of the data a user allows it to access in order to personalize content, including ads. The wording on ad personalization was broadened as well, from interests and activity to interests, activity or personalized content from Google services.

According to PPC Land, the sentence stating that Google did not show personalized ads based on content from Drive, Gmail or Photos was added in July 2021 and remained unchanged across 17 versions of the policy until the October 16 revision.

The exception is tied to Personal Intelligence, an opt-in feature that lets Search, AI Mode and Gemini draw on a user's connected apps such as Gmail and Google Photos. Google launched it in beta in the United States in January 2026 for AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers and announced an expansion to nearly 200 countries at its I/O conference in May, PPC Land reported.

Google's help page for Search says ads will not be based directly on a user's Gmail inbox or Google Photos library, and that advertisers will not have access to either. The same page says information from connected apps may also be used to show ads that are more helpful, according to PPC Land and AndroidPure. Google continues to say it does not personalize ads based on sensitive categories such as race, religion, sexual orientation or health.

AndroidPure noted that the help page leaves room for summaries and inferences drawn from connected content to inform ads, even if the raw inbox is not used. Google also says a subset of data processed by AI Mode in Search and Ask Maps is reviewed by human reviewers, and that Search services do not train generative AI models directly on the Gmail inbox but may use summaries and excerpts.

PPC Land also pointed out that the policy names Drive while the help page lists Gmail, Calendar and Photos. It added that Google confirmed around October 16 that it had begun testing ads in AI Mode for Personal Intelligence users, after saying in March 2026 that those users saw no ads.

Users who want to keep their content out of this system can disconnect apps from Personal Intelligence. AndroidPure describes the path in Google Account settings under Search Services Personalization, then Personalized Recommendations and Connected Content Apps, where Gmail, Workspace or Photos can be disconnected. Separate ad controls sit in My Ad Center.
Dexerto and SammyGuru both noted that disconnecting an app does not delete information Google has already saved in Search services history.

The change does not mean Google is scanning every inbox to sell ads. It does show how the business case for AI assistants is shifting at Google: the more personal context a user hands to Search and Gemini, the more that same context can feed the advertising business that pays for them. Keeping those two uses apart was a firm promise for five years, and it is now a conditional one.

The next thing to watch is whether Google expands ads inside AI Mode beyond its current tests, and whether regulators ask how clearly users are told that connecting Gmail or Photos to Personal Intelligence can affect the ads they see.
